title: The bow shock ahead of a sphere at low supersonic speed
question: A sphere of diameter d sits in a uniform supersonic stream of air. A detached bow shock forms ahead of it. Report where the shock crosses the axis and the shape of the shock near the axis.

conditions.gas: air, perfect gas with gamma 1.4; the stream is a free jet exhausting at atmospheric static pressure
conditions.sphere: smooth, rigidly held on a sting from behind, diameter 6.35 mm to 25.4 mm; within this range the measured quantities, divided by d, did not depend on d
conditions.reynolds_number: of order 1e4 to 1e5 on d; the shock position ahead of the sonic line was found independent of it

outputs.name: standoff_center_over_d
outputs.meaning: axial distance from the centre of the sphere to the shock on the axis, divided by d

outputs.name: shape_x_over_d_at_y_0.4
outputs.meaning: axial distance from the shock's nose to the shock at a radial distance y = 0.4 d, divided by d

practice.note: measured in the same experiment; public so that an entrant can calibrate the measurement of a shock position, not the physics

label: T2
subtitle: Leads to flag 02 · standoff and shape from Mach 1.17 to 1.81
rebuild_note: Scored with the lab's axisymmetric solver; being rebuilt natively in 3D.
